name: SHA-256 Hash Generator
description: Generate the SHA-256 hash of any text instantly using your browser's built-in Web Crypto API — the standard choice for checksums, commit hashes, and general security use.

faq.question: Why SHA-256 instead of MD5 or SHA-1?
faq.answer: SHA-256 has no known practical collision or preimage attacks, unlike MD5 and SHA-1, which is why it's the current standard for TLS certificates, Git's newer object hashing, Bitcoin's proof-of-work, and password-hashing building blocks (used inside PBKDF2/bcrypt-style schemes, not applied directly to passwords).

faq.question: How is this computed?
faq.answer: Via your browser's native Web Crypto API (crypto.subtle.digest) — the same implementation your browser uses for TLS internally, not a hand-rolled reimplementation, so results are fast and match every other correct SHA-256 implementation exactly.

faq.question: Should I hash passwords with this before storing them?
faq.answer: No. A single fast SHA-256 pass is unsuitable for password storage because it's too fast — an attacker with a leaked hash can try billions of guesses per second. Use a purpose-built, deliberately slow algorithm (bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2) on the server for that; this tool is for checksums and general-purpose hashing, not password storage.
